inline_comments.comment: `useWidth` is not a property on `TreeViewDiagramConfig` or `BaseDiagramConfig` — the valid property is `useMaxWidth`. This assignment has no effect (TypeScript should report an excess-property error here). Per project convention, new diagram config entries in `defaultConfig.ts` should explicitly set `useMaxWidth: true` to match all other diagrams (only `gitGraph` intentionally sets it to `false`). Change to `useMaxWidth: true`.

`processNode(root)` passes the artificial root node (name `"/"`, level `-1`) into `drawNode`, which calls `positionLabel` and renders the `"/"` text visibly in the SVG output. The root exists only to anchor the tree; it should never appear in the diagram. Additionally, `drawNode` draws a horizontal connecting line for the root from `x = 0 - rowIndent` (e.g. `−10`) to `x = 0`, but the `viewBox` only compensates by `−lineThickness / 2` (≈ `−0.5`), so almost all of that line is clipped. To fix both issues, skip rendering the root itself and iterate over its children: `root.children.forEach((child) => processNode(child, 0))`. Depth-0 user nodes would then draw horizontal lines from `paddingX` (positive), and the viewBox offset can be removed. You will also need to handle the vertical connecting-line logic for the root separately, since `root.BBox` will no longer be set.

`Node` is a browser-global DOM interface. Exporting a type with that name shadows it in every file that imports from `./types.js`, potentially masking real type errors or confusing readers. Use a project-scoped name such as `TreeViewNode` (which also aligns with the Langium-generated `TreeNode` from the grammar). All consumers (`db.ts`, `renderer.ts`, etc.) must be updated accordingly.

The `Common` interface, `TitleAndAccessibilities` fragment, and the `ACC_DESCR`, `ACC_TITLE`, and `TITLE` terminals are copy-pasted from the shared common grammar. Both `pie.langium` and `packet.langium` instead import `"../common/common"` at the top of the file. Using the shared import keeps definitions in sync automatically and is the established project convention. If there is a specific reason this grammar cannot import the common grammar (e.g. a token conflict), add an inline comment explaining why — per the project's Langium guidelines.

`Array.prototype.map` is used purely for its side effect (calling `db.addNode`); the returned array is discarded. Use `forEach` instead: `ast.nodes.forEach((node) => db.addNode(node.indent.length, node.name))`. This also avoids the implicit suggestion that a transformed array is being produced.

The property name `BBox` is PascalCase, which is reserved for class and type names in this codebase. Interface properties should be camelCase: rename to `bBox` or the more descriptive `boundingBox` and update all usages in `renderer.ts` and `db.ts`.

`getCount()` is declared on the `TreeViewDB` interface and implemented in `db.ts`, but is never called anywhere in the renderer or parser. This is dead code that adds surface area to the public DB interface for no benefit. Either remove `getCount` from the interface and implementation, or add a code comment explaining where it is expected to be used.
Per project naming conventions, use descriptive variable names: rename `cnt` to `count` in `TreeViewState` and update the reference in `getCount()` and `addNode()`.

The project's canonical pattern (referenced in the `pieRenderer.ts` convention) is to call `configureSvgSize` *before* setting `viewBox`. The current order sets `viewBox` first (line 118), then calls `configureSvgSize` (line 119). While `packet/renderer.ts` deviates from the rule in the same way, treeView is a new diagram and should establish correct practice: call `configureSvgSize(svg, totalHeight, totalWidth, config.useMaxWidth)` first, then set `viewBox`.
String concatenation with `+` is used to build the debug message. Per project convention, use a template literal instead: `` log.debug(`Rendering treeView diagram\n${text}`) ``.
Three consecutive blank lines at the end of the file (lines 31–33). Remove trailing blank lines to keep the file clean and consistent with the rest of the grammar files in this project.

The config properties `rowIndent`, `paddingX`, and `paddingY` represent pixel-count dimensions and should use `type: integer` (with `minimum: 0`) rather than `type: number`, per the project rule for non-negative dimension properties. `lineThickness` maps to SVG `stroke-width` which can be fractional, so `type: number` is appropriate there.

The Config Variables table documents the default for `rowIndent` as `10`, `paddingX` as `5`, etc., but there is no mention of the theme variable defaults for `fontSize` (`'16px'`) and `lineColor` (`'black'`) in context of dark/custom themes. Consider noting that `lineColor` defaults to `'black'` and may be invisible on dark-theme backgrounds, so users with dark themes will need to configure it explicitly. (Alternatively, change `styles.ts` to default to a CSS custom property or `currentColor` so it inherits from the theme.)

general_comments.comment: There is no `db.spec.ts` unit test file for the TreeView diagram. The project rules require DB-layer unit tests covering at minimum: (a) default/fallback state after `clear()`, (b) correct tree structure after `addNode()` calls with various indentation levels, and (c) edge cases such as an empty diagram, a single node, and sibling nodes at the same indentation level. The three Cypress snapshot tests exercise rendering but do not provide fast, isolated coverage of the tree-building logic in `db.ts`.

The `treeView` Langium grammar uses `SPACELIST: /\s+/` to capture node indentation. `\s+` matches any Unicode whitespace, including tabs and vertical tabs. A single tab and four spaces both produce different `indent.length` values, so users who mix or vary indentation characters will observe unexpected tree hierarchy. Consider restricting `SPACELIST` to horizontal whitespace only (e.g. `/[ \t]+/`) and documenting the supported indentation characters, or normalizing indentation before computing `indent.length` in the parser.
